title: Find All Documents
description: Retrieve every document in a collection with an empty filter.
question: Return all employee documents from the employees collection.
task: Use db.employees.find() with an empty filter to return every document.
explanation: An empty filter object matches every document in the collection. MongoDB returns documents in natural (usually insertion) order.
hints: An empty object {} matches all documents.
Call find() on the employees collection.

collection_context.description: Employee records. Each document is one employee; department_id references a department.

title: Filter by Equality
description: Match documents whose field equals a given value.
question: Find all employees who belong to department 2.
task: Return every employee document where department_id is 2.
explanation: A key-value pair in the filter document matches documents where that field equals the value.
hints: Put department_id as a key in the filter.
Use the number 2, not the string '2'.

collection_context.description: Employee records. Each document is one employee; department_id references a department.

title: Comparison Operators
description: Use $gt, $gte, $lt, and $lte to compare numeric fields.
question: Find employees whose salary is at least 10,000,000 cents.
task: Return employee documents where salary_cents is greater than or equal to 10000000.
explanation: $gte matches values greater than or equal to the given value. Other comparison operators include $gt, $lt, $lte, and $ne.
hints: Wrap the condition in an object: { $gte: value }.
Filter on salary_cents.

collection_context.description: Employee records. Salaries are stored as integer cents.

title: The $in Operator
description: Match a field against a list of allowed values.
question: Find employees in department 3 or department 4.
task: Return employee documents where department_id is either 3 or 4.
explanation: $in matches documents where the field equals any value in the provided array, similar to SQL's IN clause.
hints: Use $in with an array of values.
The array here is [3, 4].

collection_context.description: Employee records. Each document is one employee; department_id references a department.

title: Matching null Values
description: Find documents where a field is null.
question: Find employees who do not have a manager.
task: Return employee documents where manager_id is null.
explanation: Matching null in MongoDB also matches documents where the field is missing, so this returns employees with no manager_id value.
hints: Set the field's value to null in the filter.
Only the top executive should have no manager.

collection_context.description: Employee records. manager_id is null for top-level employees.

title: Combining Conditions with AND
description: Combine multiple fields in one filter to require all of them.
question: Find employees in department 2 who are still active.
task: Return employee documents where department_id is 2 and employment_status is 'Active'.
explanation: Listing multiple fields in the same filter document combines them with an implicit AND.
hints: Separate the conditions with a comma.
Status values are case-sensitive.

collection_context.description: Employee records with employment_status such as 'Active'.

title: Filtering Dates Stored as Strings
description: Compare ISO-formatted date strings with range operators.
question: Find employees hired on or after January 1, 2023.
task: Return employee documents where hire_date is on or after '2023-01-01'.
explanation: Dates here are stored as YYYY-MM-DD strings. Because that format sorts chronologically, string comparison gives the correct date order.
hints: Use $gte on hire_date.
Write the date as a string in YYYY-MM-DD format.

collection_context.description: Employee records. hire_date is stored as a YYYY-MM-DD string.

title: Pattern Matching with $regex
description: Match string fields against a regular expression.
question: Find employees whose job title contains the word 'Engineer'.
task: Return employee documents where job_title matches the pattern /Engineer/.
explanation: A regular expression in the filter matches substrings. Use /^Engineer/ to anchor the match to the start of the string.
hints: Use a /pattern/ literal as the value.
The match is case-sensitive by default.

collection_context.description: Employee records. job_title is free text.

title: Projection
description: Return only selected fields from each matching document.
question: List the first name, last name, and job title of employees in department 2.
task: Find employees in department 2 and return only first_name, last_name, and job_title. Exclude _id.
explanation: The second argument to find() is a projection. Fields set to 1 are included, and _id is included unless you set it to 0.
hints: The projection is the second argument to find().
Set _id to 0 to hide it.

title: Sorting and Limiting Results
description: Sort documents and return only the first few.
question: Find the three highest-paid employees.
task: Return first_name and salary_cents for the top 3 employees by salary, highest first.
explanation: sort() with -1 orders values from highest to lowest. limit() caps the number of results.
hints: Chain .sort() after find().
Use -1 for descending order.
Chain .limit(3) after the sort.

collection_context.description: Employee records. Salaries are stored as integer cents.

title: Counting Documents
description: Count the documents that match a filter.
question: How many employees are currently active?
task: Use countDocuments() to count employees where employment_status is 'Active'.
explanation: countDocuments() returns the number of documents matching the filter. It is the recommended replacement for the deprecated count().
hints: Use countDocuments() instead of find().
Pass the same filter you would use in find().

title: Grouping with Aggregation
description: Use $group to summarize documents by a field.
question: For each department, count the employees and sum their salaries in cents.
task: Group employees by department_id and return headcount and total_salary_cents for each group, sorted by department_id.
explanation: $group collects documents by the _id expression. $sum: 1 counts documents, and $sum on a field adds its values. Use $sort afterward to order the output.
hints: Add a $group stage with _id set to "$department_id".
Use { $sum: 1 } to count documents.
Finish with a $sort stage on _id.

collection_context.description: Employee records. Each document is one employee.

title: Match Then Group
description: Filter documents with $match before grouping.
question: Count active employees in each department.
task: Keep only active employees, group them by department_id, and return the count for each department sorted by department_id.
explanation: $match filters documents early in the pipeline, which lets later stages work on fewer documents. It works like WHERE in SQL.
hints: Start the pipeline with $match.
Group the matched documents by department_id.

title: Using $or
description: Combine conditions with $or so that documents matching any of the criteria are returned.
question: Find employees who belong to department 2 or department 3.
task: Use db.employees.find() with the $or operator to return employees where department_id is either 2 or 3.
explanation: The $or operator takes an array of expression objects and matches documents that satisfy at least one of them.
hints: Use the $or operator with an array of filter conditions.
Each condition inside the array is a separate query object.

title: Using $and
description: Combine multiple conditions explicitly using the $and operator.
question: Find employees in department 2 who earn more than 10,000,000 cents.
task: Use db.employees.find() with $and to evaluate multiple conditions explicitly.
explanation: While implicit AND is common via commas, $and is useful when applying multiple conditions to the same field or grouping complex expressions.
hints: Use $and with an array of query clauses.
Combine department_id and salary_cents checks.

title: Using $not
description: Negate a condition using the $not operator.
question: Find employees whose salary is not greater than or equal to 10,000,000 cents.
task: Use db.employees.find() with $not to negate a comparison expression on salary_cents.
explanation: $not checks for the inverse of a given query expression. Note that $not operator affects a specific field expression.
hints: Place $not inside the field condition object.
Pass an operator expression like { $gte: 10000000 } to be negated.

title: Using $in with Array Fields
description: Match documents where an array field contains any value from a specified list.
question: Find employees whose skills array contains either 'Python' or 'MongoDB'.
task: Use db.employees.find() with $in to query array fields.
explanation: When applied to an array field, $in matches documents where at least one element of the array matches any value in the $in array.
hints: Query the array field name directly.
Use { $in: [...] } to specify candidate elements.

title: Matching All Array Values
description: Use the $all operator to match arrays that contain all specified elements.
question: Find projects that include both 'Database Migration' and 'Security Audit'.
task: Use db.projects.find() with $all to match documents containing all given items in an array field.
explanation: $all selects the documents where the value of a field is an array that contains all the specified elements.
hints: Use the $all operator inside an array field condition.
Order of elements in the query array does not matter.

title: Update One Document
description: Modify a single document matching a filter using updateOne().
question: Update the job title of employee with id 10 to 'Senior Software Engineer'.
task: Use db.employees.updateOne() with $set to update a single record.
explanation: updateOne() updates the first document that matches the filter criterion. Always use update operators like $set to avoid replacing the whole document.
hints: Pass the filter as the first argument.
Use the $set update operator in the second argument.

title: Update Multiple Documents
description: Modify all matching documents using updateMany().
question: Set employment_status to 'Active' for all employees in department 7.
task: Use db.employees.updateMany() to update multiple documents at once.
explanation: updateMany() applies updates to every document matching the filter condition.
hints: Filter by department_id: 7.
Use $set to change employment_status.

title: Increment Numeric Values
description: Use the $inc operator to increment or decrement numeric fields.
question: Give all employees in department 3 a salary increase of 500,000 cents.
task: Use updateMany() with $inc on salary_cents for department 3 employees.
explanation: $inc increments a field by a specified value. Passing a negative number decrements the field.
hints: Use the $inc operator instead of $set.
Specify salary_cents and the increment amount.

title: Insert One Document
description: Add a new document to a collection using insertOne().
question: Insert a new employee record for John Doe into the employees collection.
task: Use db.employees.insertOne() to add a new employee document.
starter_query: db.employees.insertOne({ id: 29, first_name: "John", last_name: "Doe", department_id: 2, job_title: "Developer", salary_cents: 9000000, employment_status: "Active" })
solution_query: db.employees.insertOne({ id: 29, first_name: "John", last_name: "Doe", department_id: 2, job_title: "Developer", salary_cents: 9000000, employment_status: "Active" })
explanation: insertOne() inserts a single document into the collection and returns an insertion confirmation with the generated _id.
hints: Pass a document object containing employee fields into insertOne().

title: Insert Multiple Documents
description: Add multiple documents at once using insertMany().
question: Insert two new department documents into the departments collection.
task: Use db.departments.insertMany() with an array of department documents.
explanation: insertMany() takes an array of documents and inserts them in a batch.
hints: Pass an array brackets [] containing multiple JSON objects to insertMany().

title: Delete One Document
description: Remove a single document matching a filter using deleteOne().
question: Delete the employee record where id is 25.
task: Use db.employees.deleteOne() to remove a specific employee.
explanation: deleteOne() deletes the first document that matches the given filter.
hints: Pass { id: 25 } as the filter to deleteOne().

title: Delete Multiple Documents
description: Remove all documents matching a filter using deleteMany().
question: Delete all employees whose employment status is 'On Leave'.
task: Use db.employees.deleteMany() to remove all matching documents.
explanation: deleteMany() removes all documents matching the filter condition.
hints: Filter by employment_status: 'On Leave'.

title: Select Fields with $project
description: Reshape documents in an aggregation pipeline using $project.
question: Use aggregation to return only the first name and job title of employees.
task: Use db.employees.aggregate() with a $project stage to select specific fields and exclude _id.
explanation: The $project stage specifies which fields to include, exclude, or compute in the output documents of an aggregation pipeline.
hints: Include a { $project: { ... } } stage in the aggregation array.
Set _id to 0 and desired fields to 1.

title: Add Computed Fields
description: Create new fields or compute values using $addFields in an aggregation pipeline.
question: Add a computed field 'annual_salary_cents' by multiplying salary_cents by 12.
task: Use db.employees.aggregate() with $addFields to compute total annual salary.
explanation: $addFields adds new fields to documents as they pass through the pipeline without modifying the stored collection.
hints: Use $addFields with an expression like $multiply.
Reference existing fields with a dollar sign prefix, e.g., "$salary_cents".

title: Expand Arrays
description: Deconstruct an array field from the input documents to output a document for each element using $unwind.
question: Unwind the skills array from employee documents.
task: Use db.employees.aggregate() with $unwind to flatten the skills array.
explanation: $unwind transforms a document with an array into multiple documents, one for each element in the array.
hints: Pass the array field name prefixed with '$' to $unwind.

title: Join Departments
description: Perform a left outer join between employees and departments collections using $lookup.
question: Join employee records with their corresponding department documents.
task: Use db.employees.aggregate() with $lookup to join the departments collection.
explanation: $lookup performs an equality join between a collection in the same database to retrieve related documents from another collection.
hints: Specify from, localField, foreignField, and as in the $lookup stage object.

title: Join Customers and Orders
description: Join customer orders using $lookup in the aggregation pipeline.
question: Join orders into customer documents.
task: Use db.customers.aggregate() with $lookup to attach orders to each customer.
explanation: $lookup allows linking parent documents with child/related documents across different collections.
hints: Match localField to foreignField between customers and orders collections.

title: Create an Index
description: Improve query performance by creating an index on a collection field.
question: Create an ascending index on the email field of the employees collection.
task: Use db.employees.createIndex() to index the email field.
explanation: Indexes support the efficient execution of queries in MongoDB by avoiding full collection scans.
hints: Pass { email: 1 } to createIndex() for an ascending index.

title: Unique Indexes
description: Ensure uniqueness of field values across documents using a unique index.
question: Create a unique index on the email field of the employees collection.
task: Use db.employees.createIndex() with unique: true option.
explanation: A unique index ensures that the indexed fields do not store duplicate values across any documents in the collection.
hints: Pass { unique: true } as the second argument to createIndex().

title: Validate Document Structure
description: Enforce document structure validation rules using $jsonSchema.
question: Create a validator rule requiring first_name and salary_cents fields.
task: Use collMod or createCollection with validator containing $jsonSchema.
starter_query: db.createCollection("employees", { validator: { $jsonSchema: { bsonType: "object", required: ["first_name", "salary_cents"], properties: { first_name: { bsonType: "string" }, salary_cents: { bsonType: "int" } } } } })
solution_query: db.createCollection("employees", { validator: { $jsonSchema: { bsonType: "object", required: ["first_name", "salary_cents"], properties: { first_name: { bsonType: "string" }, salary_cents: { bsonType: "int" } } } } })
explanation: $jsonSchema validation enables MongoDB to enforce strict schema rules for inserted or updated documents.
hints: Use createCollection with a validator option containing $jsonSchema.
